label: Homicide Rate (per 100k, 2024–2026)
source: Secretaría de Seguridad Ciudadana CDMX / SSC + FGJ-CDMX 2024–2026
contestNote: CDMX rate is among Mexico's lowest — well below national average of ~22/100k. Critics argue femicides are systematically undercounted as homicides. Extortion complaints, by contrast, rose 21% in Jan–May 2026 (727 cases vs. 599 in 2025), showing lethal and non-lethal crime trends diverging. An ongoing Unión Tepito vs. Anti-Unión turf war in the Centro Histórico has produced 24 deaths in 2026 as of mid-August, including a 17-year-old killed Aug 10 in the Morelos/Tepito neighborhood — despite SSC reporting 55 alleged members of both factions detained in July–early August, plus 8 more (6 identified as Unión Tepito) detained in two Cuauhtémoc raids on Aug 24. Critics argue official aggregate statistics understate this street-level, zone-specific violence even as INEGI/SSC reported city-wide homicides down 16.4% (817 in 2025 vs. 978 in 2024).
delta: -57% daily homicides in June 2026 vs June 2018
deltaNote: Brugada (Jul 13, 2026): June 2026 — the World Cup opening month — closed with 1.8 daily intentional homicides, down 57% from 4.2/day in June 2018 and the lowest monthly figure in 15 years. Intentional homicides down 31% since the start of her administration; high-impact crime in H1 2026 down 64% vs. H1 2019 and 8% vs. H1 2025. SSC (Aug 3, 2026) cited INEGI data showing a 16.4% year-over-year homicide reduction (817 in 2025 vs. 978 in 2024). SSC's July 2026 strategy report (presented Aug 10) cited 464 homicide arrest warrants executed Jan–Jul 2026, up 27.8% vs. the same period in 2024 and 203% above 2019 levels, plus 217 total arrest warrants executed in 2026 (of 373 since 2024).

label: Cutzamala Reservoir Level
contestNote: Reached 90.7% in January 2026 (best in 6 years) after strong 2025 rainy season. Declined to ~77% by early May amid pre-rainy season drawdown. Still well above May 2024 historic low of 28–30%. Rainy season officially began May 15, 2026 — SACMEX deployed equipment to 56 flood-risk points citywide. A 604M peso modernization (new valves, SCADA control system) is underway after 40 years without major upgrades.
delta: Rainy season began May 15; recovery expected through June

label: Max Land Subsidence Rate
contestNote: Historic center sinking ~50cm/yr in worst zones; Palacio de Bellas Artes and Cathedral visibly tilting. Caused by groundwater over-extraction from ancient lake bed. NASA NISAR satellite data (published May 2026, Oct 2025–Jan 2026 measurements) confirmed 14 in/yr (~35 cm) at monitored landmarks including AICM airport and the Ángel de la Independencia monument.
